title: Origin of Disease and Medicine
subtitle: A story about animals, plants, and human conduct

animals.author: James Mooney
animals.locator: Myth 4 · ORIGIN OF DISEASE AND MEDICINE, normalized characters 353-760
animals.excerpt: This was bad enough, but to make it worse Man invented bows, knives, blowguns, spears, and hooks, and began to slaughter the larger animals, birds, and fishes for their flesh or their skins, while the smaller creatures, such as the frogs and worms, were crushed and trodden upon without thought, out of pure carelessness or contempt. So the animals resolved to consult upon measures for their common safety.
animals.note: Verbatim English text from Mooney's 1902 collection. Keep the specific numbered story and its East Cherokee/recorded-source context attached.

plants.author: James Mooney
plants.locator: Myth 4 · ORIGIN OF DISEASE AND MEDICINE, normalized characters 6412-6772
plants.excerpt: When the Plants, who were friendly to Man, heard what had been done by the animals, they determined to defeat the latters' evil designs. Each Tree, Shrub, and Herb, down even to the Grasses and Mosses, agreed to furnish a cure for some one of the diseases named, and each said: "I shall appear to help Man when he calls upon me in his need." Thus came medicine

narrativeBlocks.title: Animals call a council
narrativeBlocks.body: In Mooney's recorded narrative, animals complain that people hunt and kill them, and decide to meet in council.

narrativeBlocks.title: Plants respond after the animals
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from Mooney's English record (whitespace normalized): “When the Plants, who were friendly to Man, heard what had been done by the animals, they determined to defeat the latters' evil designs. Each Tree, Shrub, and Herb, down even to the Grasses and Mosses, agreed to furnish a cure for some one of the diseases named, and each said: "I shall appear to help Man when he calls upon me in his need." Thus came medicine”

narrativeBlocks.title: The story gives each plant a role
narrativeBlocks.body: The narrative says trees, shrubs, herbs, grasses, and mosses agree to provide remedies for diseases.

narrativeBlocks.title: A historical narrative, not medical advice
narrativeBlocks.body: This is Mooney's 1902 English record of a Cherokee story. It does not validate treatments or describe all present-day Cherokee medicine.

narrativeBlocks.title: The tale links human behavior and consequence
narrativeBlocks.body: The story frames disease as a response to harm done to animals and medicine as help offered by plants; keep that explanation inside this particular narrative.
